decisions.reason: SOL keeps the stopped-world image while tightening the sentence.
The split sentences preserve the distant-noise effect.
“All that had happened” preserves the scope while trimming repetition.
“Believed it” keeps the hypothetical sense.
SOL keeps the pain and its effect on his vision.
The suddenness is clear from the surrounding action; the cut is faithful.
SOL combines the confused gaze and the question's weight without dropping either.
The answer and speaker are retained in the preceding combined hunk.
“It felt natural” preserves the sense without repeating the same idea.
“Went on” preserves the continuation in natural dialogue narration.
The involuntary widening of his eyes remains clear.
The question preserves the burning pain as a possible cause.
“No” rejects pain as the reason, as the source does.
SOL preserves the wound, spreading heat, and contrast with the shock.
The hypothetical scoff and absurdity remain intact.
The truth remains unbearably cruel to him.
SOL preserves his desperate denial.
“In the first place” preserves the meaning of asking from the start.
“Added faintly” preserves the subdued delivery.
SOL preserves the enemy's admission and the Blood Lord's shiver.
The fear and opposing emotion remain distinct from defeat.
“With his whole body” conveys his embodied certainty.
The upward glance is retained in the following hunk.
SOL preserves the look up and whisper toward his heaven.
The anxiety in his heart remains; the subject is clear from context.
SOL preserves that loyalty was not his sole motive.
The master's disregard for his devoted servants remains.
The jealousy is retained in the following combined hunk.
SOL preserves his jealousy of Jin and the master's near-affection.
SOL keeps the obstacle and loyalty rationalization without adding “to his master.”
“He no longer had to” preserves that justification had become unnecessary.
“Proved for himself” keeps Jin's actions as proof of why he had to die.
“And die he would” preserves the certainty of his death.
The praise and title remain faithful.
SOL preserves the sincere whisper without changing its force.
“Inadequate” preserves the sense that the title falls short.
SOL preserves the Trance and enlightenment, using the established term.
“Fiercely” preserves the desperate fight with his life at stake.
“A handful of qi” preserves the small amount of energy and the Force terminology.
“None of that matters” preserves the dismissal of his feat.
The smile remains one a defeated man could not wear.
SOL preserves White Flame's spearhead and its position near the heart.
The tearing-flesh sound and burst of blood remain.
“Pulled free” preserves the extraction and Palm Force.
“Truly did” preserves his emphatic recollection.
“Thrust” fits the spear attack and preserves its force.
“At just that moment” preserves the timing.
SOL preserves the lost power, deviation, and implied fatal outcome.
“But he hadn’t” clearly refers to the Blood Lord not dying.
The joy welling up remains clear from the established subject.
The heavens' choice of him over Jin remains.
The transition is carried by “At that moment” in the following hunk.
SOL preserves the sudden thrill, pain forgotten, and spear-twisting action.
The shaft's violent spin and irresistible force remain.
SOL preserves the tied garment, severed cloth, and bloodied grasp.
The backward shove is retained in the following combined hunk.
SOL preserves the force driving Jin back and his fall.
Huashan and the contrast with a pond remain in the charge.
The cracked blade and thirty-six Force petals remain.
“The strike” clearly refers to the beautiful sword attack.
The desperate feeling and heartbreak remain.
The Force can cut through the petals and the forest, as in the source.
“Shook” preserves the earth's movement.
The figure's stagger and position before fallen Jin remain.
“Not one figure, but two” preserves the reveal.
SOL preserves both bloodied defenders and the Blood Lord's darkening gaze.
The raised spear and his added threat remain.
“Parted from its master” preserves their separation.
The endless rain and dark sky remain in the image.
The voice still echoing in his ears is preserved.
The joy in the Blood Lord's eyes remains the remembered image.
The statement preserves that he did all he could.
“Everything we had” preserves the group's full effort.
SOL preserves the extent to which regret or anger could no longer be felt.
The denial of following Heaven's will remains.
“Squish” fits the sound of gripping bloodied, crushed earth.
The crushed hand, bloody earth, and effort to rise remain.
SOL changes the reason for rising—“for the people” becomes a temporal condition, “not while.”
The people remain the paltry heaven the Blood Lord mocked.
“A fierce crack split the air” preserves the explosive sound.
The blurred-viewpoint action and both fighters' movements remain.
The monster's advance after clearing obstacles remains.
The Blood Lord's approaching gaze and Jin's effort to rise remain clear.
The infant image and awkward attempt to stand remain faithful.
The sun-red eyes and moment of meeting his gaze remain.
“Low, mocking laugh” preserves the audible scorn.
The sound alone still tells him what happened.
“Caught” preserves the swift wrist-grab and crushing.
The Blood Lord is clear from context; the prediction comparison is intact.
The glossary renders 회광반조 as “final rally”; SOL's unsupported capitalization makes it look like a named technique.
SOL drops the source's distinct tearing-flesh sound.
The widened eyes, look at the dagger, and lip-licking remain.
“That is why” preserves the causal setup for his threat.
“Remaining leg” preserves that this is the one still available, rather than merely the other leg.
The threat preserves that he cannot be allowed to live.
The bone bursting through mangled flesh remains.
The arm and both legs are clearly Jin's, and the throat-grab remains.
SOL preserves the shifting bones and darkening vision.
The low voice reaching him as he gasps remains.

decisions.replacement: “We’ve been bound by a long, ill-fated connection, Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung.”
